newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Metals-Weak demand prompts rise in exports.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Metals-Weak demand prompts rise in exports.

text.p: South Korean trading houses are shipping metal out of the country instead of selling it on the domestic market due to soft home demand, dealers said on Thursday.

"We have heard several trading houses are trying to sell physical (metal) overseas, especially in Southeast Asian countries, due to slow demand in the domestic market," a trader with Tong Yang Global said.
Custom office data showed South Korea's aluminium exports surged 89.4 percent to 42,075 tonnes for in the first two months of 1997 against 22,214 tonnes a year ago.
Copper exports also rose 23.9 percent in the same period to 27,215 tonnes from 21,969 tonnes a year ago.
Traders said domestic demand has been dampened by the won's steady fall against the U.S. dollar, the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel, and weeks of labour strife in January.
Another factor in the Korean metals market was the woeful state of the economy, dealers said.
South Korean Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik said on Thursday the economy was in serious trouble.
Domestic base metal prices rose this week largely on the back of the falling won, driving local buyers away from the market, traders said.

LG Metals Corp, an affiliate of LG Group and South Korea's largest copper producer, raised its monthly domestic selling price on Tuesday to 2.345 million won a tonne for April, up 48,000 won a tonne from 2.297 million won a month earlier.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were seen flat at a range of US$85-$90 a tonne CIF Pusan over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices rose to 1.53 million won a tonne this week from 1.52 million last week.
Korea Zinc, the country's largest zinc and lead producer, raised its monthly domestic zinc selling price by 90,000 won a tonne to 1.277 million won from 1.187 million won a month ago.
Korea Zinc's monthly lead price climbed to 744,000 won a tonne from 703,000 in March.
Both LG Metals and Korea Zinc's prices reflect March's LME monthly cash average prices and benchmarks for domestic physical trades.
